question.worked_solution:
To solve the equation $\sqrt{-3x-8}=x+2,$ we raise both sides to the power of $2.$  This allows us to get rid of the radical, and gives us a quadratic equation that is easier to solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{-3x-8} & =x+2 \\ {(\sqrt{-3x-8})}^{2} & =(x+2)^{2} \\ -3x-8 & ={x}^{2}+4x+4 \\ {x}^{2}+7x+12 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}+4x)+(3x+12) & =0 \\ x(x+4)+3(x+4) & =0 \\ (x+3)(x+4) & =0 \\ x & =-4,\,-3\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that in square root equations, we should always check the obtained value(s) to ensure that they are actually solutions of the original equation.

- First, we check whether the obtained value $x=-4$ is a solution of the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{-3(-4)-8} & \overset{?}{=}-4+2 \\ \sqrt{4} & \overset{?}{=}-2 \\ 2 & \ne -2\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

The value $x=-4$ does *not* satisfy the original equation, so we discard it.

- Second, we check whether the obtained value $x=-3$ is a solution of the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{-3(-3)-8} & \overset{?}{=}-3+2 \\ \sqrt{1} & \overset{?}{=}-1 \\ 1 & \ne -1\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

The value $x=-3$ does *not* satisfy the original equation, so we discard it.

Therefore, there is no solution to $\sqrt{-3x-8}=x+2x.$
